newsitem.title: SAUDI ARABIA: GCC ministers open talks on Iran ties, peace process.
newsitem.headline: GCC ministers open talks on Iran ties, peace process.

text.p: Gulf Arab foreign ministers met on Tuesday for talks on their strained ties with Iran following a tour of the six states by Iran's foreign minister, officials said.

The oil-rich Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) ministers also discussed the faltering Middle East peace process and rising Israeli-Palestinian tension after Israel's plans to build a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem, they added.
They also discussed the situation in Iraq -- their foe since Baghdad invaded Kuwait in 1990, sparking the 1991 Gulf war.
The GCC alliance groups Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Oman, Bahrain, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates.

Qatar's Foreign Minister Sheikh Hamad bin Jassim bin Jabr al-Thani, who chaired the talks, slammed Israel's groundbreaking on a Jewish housing project this month in Arab East Jerusalem that has set off clashes between Palestinians and Israeli soldiers in the West Bank.
In an opening speech, he also urged the international community to intervene to halt the plan and resume stalled Middle East peace talks.

"The Israeli government's decision to go ahead with the settlements has sabotaged the peace process, violated international resolutions, the basis of the peace process launched in Madrid in 1991 and Israeli-PLO peace accords," he said.
"We urge the international community to force Israel to commit itself to all international resolutions on Jerusalem...," said Sheikh Hamad.
It was the first such GCC meeting since the annual Gulf Arab summit in Doha in December.

Qatar, along with Oman, has already raced ahead of other GCC states in establishing economic ties with Israel but stopped short of diplomatic relations pending the resolution of the Arab-Israeli conflict.
Israel has trade missions in the two countries and Oman has opened a trade representative office in Tel Aviv.
A Gulf official said the ministers also exchanged views and information on what was discussed with Velayati in each country during his tour.
Velayati said his tour of the six states last week had opened in new chapter in relations between Iran and its Arab neighbours across the Gulf.

"In light of Dr. Velayati's tour...we hope there will be a change in Iran's language, the opening of a new page to settle all existing problems between the GCC states and Iran, and clearing the atmosphere in a frank and clear manner," Sheikh Hamad told reporters after the first round ended.

Gulf Arab states accuse Iran of interfering in their internal affairs -- a charge Iran denies -- and have voiced concern over its arms buildup. Iran says its arms programme was only for defence purposes.
Another sore point in relations is a territorial dispute over three strategic islands between Iran and the UAE.
The meeting will issue a statement at the end of its talks on Wednesday.
